name: alpenglow_cert
description: An Alpenglow consensus cert we received from a peer or constructed ourselves (see our_cert). Unparseable certs are not included. The row timestamp is when we received the cert, or constructed it if our_cert; the *_time columns are the phases that followed, each running until the next, ending at done_time. References: Table 6, Definition 12, Algorithm 1, Lemma 48

slot.description: Which slot the cert is for.

block_id.description: Which block the cert is for (only for fast_final, notar and notar_fallback, all zeros otherwise).

kind.description: What kind of cert is this.

final.description: FinalVote aggregate that sums >= 60% of stake, for slot. There is guaranteed to be one unique notarized block_id Final corresponds to.

fast_final.description: NotarVote aggregate that sums >= 80% of stake, for block_id; finalizes it in one round.

notar.description: NotarVote aggregate that sums >= 60% of stake, for block_id (BlockNotarized; Definition 15).

notar_fallback.description: NotarVote or NotarFallbackVote aggregate that sums >= 60% of stake, for block_id. At most four blocks per slot (Lemma 48).

skip.description: SkipVote or SkipFallbackVote aggregate that sums >= 60% of stake, for slot.

voters.description: Which validators' primary votes the cert aggregates (NotarVote for notar, fast_final and notar_fallback; FinalVote for final; SkipVote for skip), as a bitmap over the voter's rank in the slot's epoch: rank r is bit r%8 of byte r/8, bytes through the highest signer.

fallback_voters.description: Fallback signer set (NotarFallbackVote for notar_fallback, SkipFallbackVote for skip), a bitmap by rank like voters. Empty for other kinds.

relayer_ip.description: IPv4 address of the peer that relayed the cert to us; ourselves if our_cert, stored as an IPv4-mapped IPv6 address (all zeros if unknown).

relayer_identity.description: Validator identity of the peer that relayed the cert to us (determined from the QUIC client-side TLS certificate); ourselves if our_cert (all zeros if unknown_peer). Not necessarily the creator of the cert: a node re-broadcasts the first valid cert it obtains (whether from self or others).

our_cert.description: Whether we constructed the cert ourselves from the votes we had received, rather than a peer delivering it first. Not every cert is self-made; when it is, we reached the threshold before any peer's copy arrived, i.e. we are running fast.

broadcast_reason.description: Why we broadcast the cert (based on the Alpenglow certificate rules, see Table 6 and Definition 13) (not_broadcasted if we did not).

not_broadcasted.description: We did not broadcast the cert for various reasons, see processing_result.

first_valid.description: The first valid cert of its kind for the slot that we received or constructed; every node broadcasts these (Definition 13).

broadcast_to.description: Who we sent the cert to, indexed by rank like voters: identity and address at each rank, all zeros where we did not send (only if broadcast_reason is first_valid, empty otherwise).

identity.description: Validator identity of the peer (all zeros if not sent).

ip.description: IPv4 address of the peer as an IPv4-mapped IPv6 address (all zeros if not sent).

port.description: Port of the peer's Alpenglow QUIC endpoint (0 if not sent).

processing_result.description: What we did with the cert. unknown_peer and banned_peer are decided on the connection before the cert is decoded, shred_version_mismatch and unranked_peer after decoding, in that order; the rest are Alpenglow-specific.

unknown_peer.description: The connection had no known peer: we cleared its identity while closing it, or accepted it before we knew the epoch's validators.

banned_peer.description: The peer is banned for an earlier invalid signature or cert; connection closed.

shred_version_mismatch.description: Signed under a different shred version than ours.

unranked_peer.description: The peer has no rank in the slot's epoch.

slot_too_old.description: The slot is behind our finality frontier, or in an earlier epoch we have no stake information for.

slot_too_new.description: The slot is beyond our look-ahead window, or in an epoch we have no stake information for.

duplicate.description: We already held a cert of this kind for the slot, or for this block if notar_fallback; we keep one per kind (Definition 13), so we dropped the copy without verifying it. The common case: every node broadcasts each cert it accepts. Recorded for notar certs only.

ignored_redundant.description: We already hold a valid cert that supersedes this one, e.g. a fast-finalization cert for the block a notarization cert arrives for; ignored.

failed_bls_verify.description: The signers' stake is below the threshold (Table 6), a signer rank is outside the epoch, or the aggregate BLS signature is invalid; peer banned.

accepted.description: BLS verified (stake threshold of Table 6 and aggregate BLS signature) and stored as the first cert of its kind for the slot, then broadcast to our peers (Definition 13); see broadcast_start_time and broadcast_to.

verify_start_time.description: When we started BLS verifying the cert (unset if our_cert).

broadcast_start_time.description: When we started broadcasting the cert to our peers, BLS verification having finished (only if broadcast_reason is first_valid, 0 otherwise).

done_time.description: When we finished processing the cert, may be any of the above stages including short-circuiting at earlier stages.
